Two transactions are "not-interleaved" in a schedule if every action of one transaction precedes every action of the other.
We say that a transaction TT precedes a transaction UU in a schedule SS if they are not interleaved, and all actions of TT precedes all actions of UU in S.S.

Note that if TT and UU are the Only transactions in SS, then saying TT precedes UU is the same as saying that SS is the serial schedule (T,U).(T,U).

However, if SS involves transactions other than TT and U,U, then SS might not be a serial schedule, in fact, because of the effect of other transactions, SS might not even be conflict-serializable.
